props.title: Never Been Kissed
props.initialSlug: Undercover reporter relives high school, finds love

sections.content: Never Been Kissed perfectly captures Y2K-era teen comedy while adding depth through its unique "second chance" premise. Drew Barrymore shines as Josie Geller, a copy editor who goes undercover at high school, confronting her traumatic teen years while falling for her English teacher (Michael Vartan). It follows the DNA of teen makeover films like She's All That (1999) and Clueless (1995), but flips the script by examining high school through both teenage and adult perspectives. The film's genius lies in parallel humiliations - Josie's past as "Josie Grossie" and her present fumbles - creating genuine emotional stakes rare in the genre.

sections.content: The film arrived at peak teen movie renaissance, alongside 10 Things I Hate About You (1999) and Drive Me Crazy (1999). But while those stayed firmly in teenage territory, Never Been Kissed explored millennial anxiety about adulting and second chances. Its DNA influenced later films like 13 Going on 30 (2004) and 17 Again (2009), where adult perspectives crash into teenage worlds. The fish-out-of-water comedy works because Barrymore commits fully to both Josie's awkwardness and her gradual self-discovery.

Director Raja Gosnell brings surprising depth to what could have been a shallow concept. The romantic tension between Josie and Mr. Coulson predates similar teacher-student dynamics in A Teacher (2020) but handles it with appropriate restraint given the comedy format. The film's exploration of sibling relationships through Josie and Rob (David Arquette) adds welcome complexity, while supporting performances from Molly Shannon and John C. Reilly provide sharp comedic edges. SUBHEAD: Impact on Teen Comedy Evolution

sections.content: Never Been Kissed marked a crucial transition in teen comedies, bridging the gap between the pure high school stories of Can't Hardly Wait (1998) and the more mature explorations of young adulthood in films like Garden State (2004). Its influence can be seen in later works like 21 Jump Street (2012), which similarly placed adults back in high school but with a more satirical edge. The film's treatment of trauma and redemption through comedy became a template for smart teen films like Easy A (2010) and The Edge of Seventeen (2016).
